newsitem.title: BOSNIA: US bid for Bosnian's sacking not tied to Iran.
newsitem.headline: US bid for Bosnian's sacking not tied to Iran.

text.p: The Bosnian government on Saturday denied a deputy defence minister's links to Iran were behind a United States demand for his dismissal, state radio reported.

The Sarajevo government's failure to sack Hasan Cengic has blocked the delivery of a $100 million arms shipment bound for the Moslem-Croat federation army as part of the U.S.-backed "Train and Equip"" programme.
A chartered freighter carrying the bulk of the arms shipment for the federation left the port of Ploce in neighbouring Croatia on Saturday without unloading its cargo.

A statement from the office of Bosnia's Moslem president Alija Izetbegovic said that the United States had asked last month by letter for the removal of Cengic, but not because of his alleged contacts with Iran.
Washington complained of Cengic's "insufficient cooperativeness in making and carrying out the federation's defence law", and recommended he be fired, the statement said.
"But we know for sure that a similar request has been made with regards to the (Croat) minister of defence Vladimir Soljic", the statement added.
"An "Iranian connection' or something similar is not the reason for the American request," the statement went on.

U.S. officials have said the cargo vessel, now off the Croatian coast, will not unload its shipment of tanks, helicopters and guns until the Bosnian government in Sarajevo fires Cengic, but it has not specified why it wants him to go.
Cengic appeared to be in his office on Saturday, receiving a military delegation from Turkey.
The controversial "Train and Equip" programme is designed to give the Moslems and Croats military parity with well-armoured Serb forces.

But its start was long delayed by reluctance from both Moslem and Croats, who fought a bitter war throughout 1993, to merge their forces in one army. Agreement on a unified army was reached recently after months of squabbling.
Analysts said the Bosnian government appeared to be clearing the way for Cengic's removal by denying his alleged Iranian links.

The statement said that there were some other difficulties regarding the weapons delivery that have nothing to do with defence minister and his deputy, but that Izetbegovic was confident those difficulties would be overcome soon.
